breakpoints.gap: Wrote the sideways part as T·cosθ. Vertical = T·cosθ, horizontal = T·sinθ.
Wrote a = g × θ. It is a = g·tanθ (g·θ only for small angles in radians).
Did not define it: 4 motor inputs, 6 degrees of freedom, so sideways force needs a tilt first.
Did not know the unit: m/s² (velocity in m/s, changing every second).
Said raise position gains. A constant extra weight leaves a steady sag under P; higher gains shrink it but never remove it. The integral term of the vertical velocity loop removes it.

breakpoints.topic: Chinese: A 是 B 的 C
breakpoints.gap: Reversed the order (内环的速度环) and used wrong characters (自胎换, 内魂). Correct: 姿态环是速度环的内环。
For a=(0,2,0) wrote T=3*2=6 N. Gravity must be added first: T=m*sqrt(ax^2+ay^2+(az+g)^2)=30.04 N.
Thought theta/phi are pitch/roll. theta = total lean from vertical, phi = lean direction; roll and pitch split that lean into two axes.

breakpoints.topic: Chinese: 速度环 vs 角速度环
breakpoints.gap: Rate loop is 角速度环 (angular rate), 速度环 is the velocity loop. Order A是B的C now correct.
Wrote formulas without computing (g*tan25 = 4.57 m/s^2, theta = 11.5 deg, phi = 90 deg). Always finish with number + unit.
Grill Q1/Q6: labelled 15.66 N as m/s^2 and 4.905 N as metres. Carry units: N / (N/m) = m, so sag = 4.905/6 = 0.82 m.
Grill Q1: fed T into the 3-D formula (27.71 N). Holding height means vertical part = weight = 14.72 N; correct T 15.66 N, horizontal 5.36 N, a 3.57 m/s^2.
Grill Q4: phi = atan2(ay, ax) = atan2(0, -1) = 180 deg (all pitch, backward), not -90. T also wrong: 22.71 N, not 12.35.
Grill Q2: 40 deg = 0.698 rad (x pi/180), so g*theta = 6.85 m/s^2, not 2.81.

breakpoints.topic: why the integral holds at zero error
breakpoints.gap: Grill Q6c: named the I term but not why: its output is the stored sum of past error, so it stays put when e = 0.
Grill Q7: velocity is not from a laser (laser rangefinder = height only). It is estimated: GNSS/RTK + IMU, optical flow or camera. Units m/s vs rad/s missing.
Grill Q8: wrote the chain in English and skipped the A是B的C sentences. Still open from L01 Q4.
Own-words: said the velocity loop differentiates the setpoint. It runs PID on velocity error (desired - measured) and its output is the desired acceleration.
Own-words: described yaw as 'orthogonal axes'. Diagonal pairs spin the same way; speeding up one pair turns the body the opposite way (reaction torque); total thrust unchanged.
Own-words: did not say the rate loop outputs 3 torques, or that total thrust T goes from the acceleration step straight to the mixer (4 inputs -> 4 motors).
Own-words: called the lean direction phi the 'heading'. Heading is yaw psi. Standard notation phi/theta/psi = roll/pitch/yaw clashes with the lesson's theta/phi.
Own-words: summary ran thrust -> tilt -> acceleration. The controller computes T and tilt both from the desired acceleration; physics runs the other way. Also squared az+g in the atan2.
